    ====Noun==== bye (plural [[:byes#English|byes]])[[Category:English lemmas|BYE]][[Category:English nouns|BYE]][[Category:English countable nouns|BYE]][[Category:English entries with incorrect language header|BYE]][[Category:Pages with entries|BYE]][[Category:Pages with 10 entries|BYE]] # ([[computing#Noun|computing]][[Category:en:Computing|BYE]]) A [[command]] to exit a [[session]]. ===Etymology 3=== ====Noun==== bye (plural [[:byes#English|byes]])[[Category:English lemmas|BYE]][[Category:English nouns|BYE]][[Category:English countable nouns|BYE]][[Category:English entries with incorrect language header|BYE]][[Category:Pages with entries|BYE]][[Category:Pages with 10 entries|BYE]] # [[Appendix:Glossary#eye_dialect|Eye dialect]] spelling of [[:boy#English|boy]][[Category:English eye dialect|BYE]]. #*
    '''1883''', Rose Garfield Clemens, “Pat and the Pig”, in Ballou's Dollar Monthly Magazine, volume 58, page 383:[[Category:English terms with quotations|BYE]]
    "So what shall I do, now, Patric? Can you think of any plan? "Bedad!" said Pat , as he scratched his head , “ I'm the very '''bye''' that can."
    [[Category:English terms with quotations|BYE]]
    #*
    '''1887''', “Pat's Love Episode”, in Parry's Monthly Magazine, volume 3, page 252:[[Category:English terms with quotations|BYE]]
    'Och,' sez I, 'there's many a '''bye''' that's lonely livin' rite wid his friends an' naybors. Sure an' I'm lonesome mesilf.'
    [[Category:English terms with quotations|BYE]]
    #*
    '''1903''', Our Young People - Volume 12, page 51:[[Category:English terms with quotations|BYE]]
    There a '''bye''' has his hand toorn off, and there a '''bye''' loses his eyesight complately, and over yan a '''bye''' has his joogular vein torn wid a whistlin' boom, and forninst that is the '''bye''' who thinks his gun isn't loaded and kills his little sisther.
    [[Category:English terms with quotations|BYE]]
    #*
    '''1907''', International Molders' and Foundry Workers' Journal, page 545:[[Category:English terms with quotations|BYE]]
    In thim days the '''bye''' who wint to work in the foundhry to learn the thrade, in goin' into the shop in the morning would meet a big, ruffneck boss wit his blue faunel shirt on and his schleeves rolled up to his ilbows, who could show him the mishtakes he made the day befoor, if he made any.
    [[Category:English terms with quotations|BYE]]
    #*
    '''1920''', Marjorie Benton Cooke, The Girl who Lived in the Woods, page 184:[[Category:English terms with quotations|BYE]]
    I know a nice '''bye''' who's goin' to git two cookies fer thim worrds.
    [[Category:English terms with quotations|BYE]]
    #*
    '''2012''', Robert Craig Brown, Illustrated History of Canada, page 224:[[Category:English terms with quotations|BYE]]
    Hardy, weatherbeaten, intimately familiar with the winds and tides of his local shore, capable of turning his hand to many things, squeezing a hard living from the treacherous sea—a figure rendered familiar by the words “Ise the '''bye''' who builds the boat / And ise the '''bye''' that sails her / Ise the '''bye''' who catches the fish / And takes them home to Liza."
    [[Category:English terms with quotations|BYE]]
